approval_timeline.complex: 1-3 weeks for standard plan review; longer if fire/life-safety, accessibility, occupancy load, or historic district review is involved.
approval_timeline.simple: Commercial TI/addition/remodel scopes usually require plan review; expect at least several business days to a few weeks depending on completeness, valuation, and local queue.

checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in LA
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Occupancy reclassification: identify existing approved occupancy + proposed group; require code-official approval + new/updated Certificate of Occupancy (IEBC §§1001.1, 1001.2, 1001.3; IBC Ch. 3)
Height/area limit recheck: compare new occupancy hazard category to existing construction type, allowable area, frontage/sprinkler increases, fire-wall strategy (IEBC §1011.5; IBC Ch. 5)

Fire-resistance + separation reassessment: re-verify fire barriers, horizontal assemblies, exterior wall ratings/openings, shaft enclosures, mixed-occupancy separations for the new hazard category (IEBC §§1011.1, 1011.5.3, 1011.6/7; IBC Ch. 7)
monitoring requirements at the new occupancy + IBC/IFC Ch. 9 thresholds (IEBC §§1004.1, 1011.2; IFC Ch. 9)

Means of egress recalculation: occupant load + number of exits + egress capacity + travel distance + common path + dead ends + door hardware updated to new occupancy (IEBC §§1005.1, 1011.4; IBC Ch. 10)
Accessibility / path-of-travel trigger: alterations to primary-function areas trigger ADA upgrades to altered area + serving amenities (2010 ADA §202.4 + 28 CFR §36.403)

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed Louisiana contractor pulls the permit on the owner/operator's behalf, and the contractor's state license number must appear on the application. For HVAC work, New Orleans also requires a Class A City of New Orleans HVAC license if HVAC is added later. The permit is still required for the occupancy change and trade work.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of New Orleans Department of Safety & Permits
response_body.city_contractor_registration: New Orleans uses the One Stop App contractor status system. Contractors should verify their current contractor status in the portal before submitting. If the contractor's city status is expired or inactive, the application can be blocked until renewed.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to separate the electrical and plumbing scope values from the building valuation — the city fee is based on construction value and the trade permits need the correct valuation
Starting demolition or framing before the permit is issued and posted — New Orleans can issue stop-work orders and require re-submittal

Submitting permit application without verifying current contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the City of New Orleans One Stop App portal at (use the Inspections/Your Items functions after permit issuance). Phone: (504) 658-7100. Advance notice requirement was not stated in the source context; verify current lead time with the inspector assigned to your permit before covering work. inspections.description: Inspector checks occupancy layout, exit access, door swing and egress width, rated separations if required, accessibility clearances, fire extinguisher locations if shown on plans, and that any framing or wall changes match approved plans.
inspections.timing: Before walls are closed and before finishes are installed

inspections.description: Inspector verifies new branch-circuit routing, box fill, conductor sizing, grounding and bonding, panel schedule, required GFCI/AFCI where applicable, equipment disconnects, and that commercial receptacle and lighting layout matches approved plans.
inspections.timing: Before insulation, drywall, or ceiling closure

inspections.description: Inspector checks water and waste piping layout, venting, fixture rough locations, trap arm lengths, cleanouts, pipe support, and test pressure before concealment.
inspections.timing: Before walls, ceilings, or slab trenches are covered

inspections.description: Inspector confirms all fixtures, devices, signage-related penetrations, emergency lighting/egress lighting if required, GFCI protection, panel labeling, plumbing fixture operation, leak-free drains, and that the space matches the approved change-of-occupancy plans.
inspections.timing: After all work is complete and before opening for business

Use the One Stop App contractor status check before you start the application so you do not lose a day to a lapsed city registration
exit paths clearly — that is where commercial change-of-use reviews usually slow down

what_to_bring: Completed commercial permit application in One Stop App with project valuation broken out by building, electrical, and plumbing scope
Signed and sealed plan set showing existing and proposed floor plan, occupancy classification, occupant load, egress, accessibility, and fixture layout
Contractor Louisiana state license information and city contractor status confirmation
Property address, suite/unit information, and owner authorization letter if filing for the owner
Equipment and fixture cut sheets for any new electrical equipment, plumbing fixtures, and any code-related life-safety devices shown on the plans
If the property is in a historic district or flood zone, bring the historic review approval and any elevation/flood documentation
response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Commercial change-of-occupancy work in New Orleans may be affected by zoning, parking, alcohol-related use approvals, and historic district overlays. If the property is in the French Quarter, CBD, or another historic district, HDLC/Vieux Carré review can add time and a 50% permit fee surcharge.
